$comment: Scenarios where KovaaK's own aim type is wrong, and the measurement that says so. KovaaK's /scenario/popular is authoritative for Clicking / Tracking / Switching and is preferred over everything else by tools/generate_seed.py, because a benchmark author's category name is a sub-category as often as a category and guessing from a description was measurably wrong on 6 of Voltaic's 18. That preference is right. It is not infallible, and where it is wrong the error is not cosmetic: aim_type is the column find-match partitions the queue on, so a scenario mislabelled here is graded by the season as one skill and matched as another.
$rule: A correction needs a measurement, not an opinion. The discriminator is shots per kill, taken from the kill table of real runs: a clicking scenario fires once per target and a sustained-fire scenario fires tens or hundreds of times. It separates the corpus cleanly with two orders of magnitude between the groups and nothing in between, which is why it can carry a correction that overrides a first-party source. npm run validate:aimtypes re-derives every figure below from the stats folder and fails if the gap has closed.
$refusals: Two things this must not become. It is not a place to file a scenario whose category is merely debatable - the measurement has to put it outside the range of the type KovaaK's assigned, not merely near the edge. And a correction that agrees with KovaaK's is refused rather than ignored, because a correction nobody is checking is how a wrong label becomes permanent.

measurement.statistic: shots per kill, summed over every kill row in every local run whose filename begins '<scenario> - '. The exact prefix matters: matching '<scenario>*' instead sweeps in every variant sharing the stem, which is how the first draft of these figures had VT DotTS Intermediate S5 at 33.6 over 28,299 kills rather than 40.5 over 5,184.
measurement.source: the KovaaK's stats folder, parsed by src/core/stats/parseStatsFile.ts

reference.$comment: The ranges the discriminator separates, measured on scenarios whose aim type nobody disputes.

domiSwitch.why: 177 shots per kill against the 1.1 to 1.3 every clicking scenario in the corpus produces - a factor of about 140, and further from clicking than the target-switching scenarios are. The weapon is a Poke-Drill and the bot is a regen_dot: the target has 55 health and regenerates 0.3s after damage stops, so a single click cannot eliminate anything and the score is decided by how much of the time the crosshair is on a target. That is not a clicking scenario under any reading. Four benchmarks that name it - Aimerz+ Evasive Switching, both Viscose seasons and snakbox - all file it under evasive switching, and the community thread cited in scenario_rationale.json names it as one of the two evasive-switching references.
domiSwitch.note: KovaaK's appears to classify by trigger rather than by mechanic: every scenario in Aimerz+ Evasive Switching that carries an aim type at all carries Clicking, including Star Tracking Regen, while the tamTargetSwitch scenarios in the same tier carry none. This corrects the two the pool and its neighbours actually use rather than the group, because a measurement was taken for these two and not for the rest.

domiSwitch Easy.why: The same scenario with larger or slower targets, measured over 1,900 kills, and the same 136 shots per kill. Corrected alongside its sibling because leaving it would put one half of a lineage in Clicking and the other in Switching, which is worse than either answer on its own: the weakness map and the sub-skill queues read this column, and a lineage split across two categories is invisible to both.
